title: The Midnight Library
author: Matt Haig
description: Between life and death there is a library, and within that library, the shelves go on forever. Every book provides a chance to try another life you could have lived. Nora Seed finds herself in this magical place and must decide what really makes a life worth living.

title: Clean Code
author: Robert C. Martin
description: A handbook of agile software craftsmanship that teaches developers how to write readable, maintainable, and elegant code. Full of practical advice and real-world examples that transform messy code into clean, professional software.

title: A Brief History of Time
author: Stephen Hawking
description: From the Big Bang to black holes, Stephen Hawking explores the universe's greatest mysteries in plain language. A landmark work of popular science that changed how millions of people think about space, time, and the cosmos.

title: The Alchemist
author: Paulo Coelho
description: A young Andalusian shepherd named Santiago travels from Spain to the Egyptian desert in search of treasure. Along the journey he discovers that the real treasure lies within himself — a timeless tale of following your dreams.

title: The Pragmatic Programmer
author: David Thomas & Andrew Hunt
description: A collection of tips and best practices for software development that remain relevant across languages and frameworks. Covers everything from personal responsibility to career development, coding techniques, and team dynamics.

title: Sapiens: A Brief History of Humankind
author: Yuval Noah Harari
description: A sweeping narrative of humanity's creation and evolution, exploring how biology and history have defined us. Examines how the cognitive revolution, agricultural revolution, and unification of humankind shaped the world we live in today.

title: To Kill a Mockingbird
author: Harper Lee
description: Set in the American South during the 1930s, this Pulitzer Prize-winning novel follows young Scout Finch as her father, lawyer Atticus Finch, defends a Black man unjustly accused of a crime. A powerful exploration of race, justice, and childhood innocence.

title: You Don't Know JS
author: Kyle Simpson
description: A deep dive into the core mechanisms of JavaScript. This series challenges common assumptions about the language and teaches developers to truly understand how JS works under the hood — from scope and closures to async and performance.

title: The Gene: An Intimate History
author: Siddhartha Mukherjee
description: A fascinating exploration of the history and science of the gene, from Gregor Mendel's peas to CRISPR gene editing. Mukherjee weaves together science, history, and ethics to explain how genes define us and what their manipulation means for our future.

author: George Orwell
description: In a totalitarian future society, Winston Smith works for the Party rewriting historical records. His forbidden love affair and growing rebellion against Big Brother leads to devastating consequences in this chilling dystopian masterpiece.

title: Designing Data-Intensive Applications
author: Martin Kleppmann
description: A comprehensive guide to the principles and practicalities of building reliable, scalable, and maintainable data systems. Covers databases, distributed systems, streaming, and the trade-offs engineers face when designing modern applications.

title: The Selfish Gene
author: Richard Dawkins
description: Richard Dawkins introduces the gene-centered view of evolution and coins the term 'meme' in this revolutionary work of science. A thought-provoking argument that genes — not individuals or species — are the true units of natural selection.
